title: Variant handshake lattice: tokenizer/context/tooling parity maintenance
creator: Luca Ortega
description: Maintenance and refresh of the fallback model variant compatibility lattice (handshake matrix) to ensure tokenizer, context-window semantics, and operator tooling remain compatible across active model variants used by smart routing policies.
background: Smart routing may reroute requests across regions, tiers, and model variants during load, outage, or cost-optimization events. Our fallback logic assumes variants are interoperable for tokenization, context slicing, and tooling (e.g., function-call ABI, structured output markers). Over time we've observed drift: token boundary mismatches, off-by-one context handling, and tooling version skew that cause degraded outputs and silent failures during rollouts.
goals: Produce a canonical compatibility lattice (human + machine-readable) that covers tokenizer behavior, context-window semantics, and runtime tooling expectations for all production variants
Automate nightly handshake tests and surface regressions to Runtime SRE and Model Onboarding teams
Create remediation playbooks for common mismatch classes (tokenizer drift, context truncation, tooling ABI mismatch)
Integrate pruning rules into the smart router so incompatible fallbacks are excluded at decision time
scope: All active hosted and dedicated model variants referenced by smart routing policies
Tokenizer normalization and special token semantics (pad, bos, eos, tool markers)
Context window alignment checks (effective seq length, off-by-one behavior)
Tooling/ABI expectations: function calling JSON schema, streaming boundaries, chunked KV cache compatibility
out_of_scope: Rewriting model tokenizers or retraining models
Private (on-prem) variant upgrades — those will be covered in a separate private-deployment checklist
Large-scale model onboarding (we will surface failing variants to model onboarding but not perform model-side fixes in this task)
proposal: Define a compatibility lattice file (YAML/CSV canonicalized) that enumerates pairwise handshake properties between variant A and variant B. Implement an automated test harness that runs a small but targeted test corpus (tokenization edge-cases, prefix-preservation, function-call framing) and reports a pass/fail and failure class (tokenizer, context, tooling). Wire results to a daily CI job and add a gating check for router config changes.
implementation_steps: Design the compatibility lattice spec (columns: variant_a, variant_b, tokenizer_eq, ctx_behavior, tool_abi, kv_cache_compatible, last_tested)
Create a micro harness 'handshake-tester' in runtime/ci that spins up lightweight variant docker/containers and runs the corpus
Curate a focused corpus of ~120 test vectors covering: whitespace handling, unicode edge cases, long-context boundary triggers, function-call framing, structured output delimiters
Run sweep across current active variants and generate the first lattice snapshot
Surface failures and classify them; create remediation tickets for top failure classes
Add a pruning layer to smart router config that marks incompatible fallbacks as ineligible for automated reroute
Add nightly scheduled job and alerting to #runtime-compat-alerts Slack channel and to the Runtime SRE dashboard
Document the lattice format and remediation playbooks in the Runtime Handbook and link from Console rollout UI
acceptance_criteria: A canonical lattice file exists in runtime/handshake/lattice-YYYYMMDD.csv and contains pairwise statuses for all active variants
The handshake-tester CI job runs in <= 45 minutes for full sweep and populates shard results into CI artifacts
Router pruner correctly excludes any fallback marked as 'tool_abi=false' or 'tokenizer_eq=false' during rollouts in the staging environment
At least 90% of currently failing pairwise checks have an assigned remediation ticket or a documented mitigation
On-call and SRE teams receive alerts for new failures and can view failure diffs via the CI artifact
testing_plan: Unit tests for lattice parser and pruner logic, end-to-end handshake-tester runs in a sandboxed k8s job, manual verification of router behavior in staging with synthetic traffic. Include regression harness for downstream SDK/tooling integration tests.
monitoring: Create Prometheus metrics: handshake_test_runs_total, handshake_failures_total, handshake_failure_by_class{class="tokenizer"|"context"|"tooling"}, handshake_age_seconds (time since last successful sweep). Add dashboard panels to Runtime SRE dashboard and configure PagerDuty escalation for sudden spikes in failures.
rollout_steps: Deploy handshake-tester to CI and run a full sweep (non-blocking) for initial baseline
Review baseline with Model Onboarding and Runtime SRE, triage failures
Deploy router pruner to staging behind feature flag — reject incompatible fallbacks during canary reroutes
Run controlled canary and verify no silent degradation; rollback if tooling-related failures observed
Flip feature flag for production after 2 successful canary days and no new critical failures
docs_required: Runtime handbook: compatibility lattice spec and failure classes
Runbook: how to triage tokenizer drift and context truncation
Console: short note in Rollouts docs explaining why certain variants may be excluded from fallback lists
risks_and_mitigation: False positives in handshake tests could reduce available fallbacks — mitigation: conservative pruning defaults to only exclude on confirmed tooling or tokenizer mismatch and allow manual override
Test corpus may not cover real-world prompt distributions — mitigation: integrate sampled production prompts (anonymized) into nightly fuzz corpus
Router performance impact from doing more checks — mitigation: lattice lookups are cached and evaluated during config change, not per-request
